brief: The Market Ear argues gold is set up for a possible bounce. Gold trades unusually far below its 200-day moving average, non-commercial speculators have aggressively cut net long gold exposure over the past two months, and CTAs are running sizeable gold shorts near levels that have historically triggered short-covering reversals; GS CTA projections show this cohort needing to buy gold irrespective of scenario. Separately, the dollar (which moves inversely with gold) is stretched versus its own 200-day moving average and just posted its biggest down candle in a while as it nears a descending trendline in place since mid-2023, which could mean a dollar pause. CTAs are simultaneously long the dollar and short gold, so reversing both could drive gold sharply higher. On demand, SocGen estimates Tether has been the world's fifth-largest net buyer of gold since 2023 (87.5 tonnes through June 2026, holdings growing 31% annually versus 13.6% for gold ETFs and 1.8% for central banks), with about 65% of inflows into Tether's gold products estimated as new money rather than reallocation. The piece poses this as a case for a near-term bounce, not a certainty.
